objective: Review the process-to-launcher CLI boundary definition and decide whether a scoped non-executing fixture implementation may connect a Verilator-facing parser payload to the existing sidecar launcher CLI argv without claiming direct Verilator sidecar execution.

review_decision.reason: The definition is narrow enough for a scoped fixture implementation because it explicitly separates parser schedule, sidecar context, source or template authority, structured launcher argv, stage execution, compare execution, and timing evidence before any process-to-launcher CLI connection may be claimed.
review_decision.weakest_point: The definition still does not implement a Verilator-facing process-to-launcher connection. The accepted predecessor only proved structured run_hybrid_template.py invocation from reviewed metadata; the next implementation must not turn parser payloads, generated command text, or template-run evidence into execution authority.
accepted_because: the boundary starts from reviewed structured launcher invocation evidence without over-reading it as direct Verilator execution
the future connection remains scoped to pulp_ita_mha, config/slice_launch_templates/pulp_ita_mha.json, and 64x1
the required native option spelling, target, template, shape, and launcher argv are explicit
payload-only execution authority and generated command text authority are rejected
parser, context, authority, bridge, launcher, stage, compare, and timing failure classes remain distinct
generated reports and artifacts remain noncanonical

required_next_gate.name: implement_verilator_native_option_parser_direct_command_path_native_invocation_process_to_launcher_cli_fixture_gate
must_implement: a scoped non-executing fixture that validates parser payload, explicit sidecar context, and source or template authority before materializing launcher CLI argv
structured output that records whether the process-to-launcher CLI bridge is ready while keeping launcher invocation false
target, template, shape, state count, and step count cross-checks before argv construction
explicit rejection of payload-only execution authority and generated command text authority
preserved failure classes for process parse, context, authority, bridge, launcher, stage, compare, and timing-without-measurement

non_claims: not broad native Verilator option support
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
